summary: Forest Service L-4 cab on a 20-foot pole tower above Timberline (1933), used in place of the summit lookout; burned in May 1963; a footprint remains.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 20-foot pole tower (1933); a stone supply cabin stood on the site from 1922
facts.status_note: Burned in May 1963 per The Oregonian, as quoted by Forest Lookouts; the register says removed in 1964; a hiking guide's photos show a footprint and captions note nails, glass, metal parts and anchors
facts.access: Walking access per WillhiteWeb: take the Magic Mile lift up and hike down the road, or walk up the access road from Timberline Lodge. No official source on public access was found.

corrections.why: The register describes a 20-foot pole L-4 tower and firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb describe an L-4 cab, so the structure was not a ground lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1963 Oregonian report, quoted on Forest Lookouts, says the Forest Service burned the lookout down. The register says removed in 1964 and firelookout.com says destroyed in 1964. The story follows the 1963 report, which is closest to the event, and gives both 1964 dates as the register's and firelookout.com's versions.

sources.title: Lone Fir Rock Lookout Site Mount Hood

notes_for_editor: The register's '20' pole' is read as the tower height (6.1 m); the register does not say whether 20 ft is the cab or the pole height. The fate follows the 1963 Oregonian report as quoted by Forest Lookouts; the register (removed 1964) and firelookout.com (destroyed 1964) disagree. Today's remains rest on one hiking guide's photos (WillhiteWeb); no official source describes the site now. Coordinates and elevation match the record (register: N 45.340720, W 121.712480; 2,012 m). The WillhiteWeb page gives walking access (Magic Mile lift and hike down the road, or the access road from Timberline Lodge). The story now mentions this in one sentence and states that no source found says whether the public may visit; the step-by-step route is not in the story.
